---
name: photocraft
description: "."
applications:
  - id: photocraft
    role: primary
---

PhotoCraft edits layered PSD and PSB files headlessly.
Use PhotoCraft only when the user names it or chose it as their default; never as a fallback or a stand-in for another tool.

PhotoCraft's standalone CLI is independent of its desktop app. The pinned release is
[v0.6.0](https://github.com/storytold/photocraft/releases/tag/v0.6.0).
Install the CLI on demand, without admin rights, into
`$VOYAGER_HOME/tools/photocraft/0.6.0`. The macOS asset is
`photocraft-cli-0.6.0-macos-universal.zip`; extract with `ditto -x -k`.
Its binary is `photocraft-cli-0.6.0-macos-universal/photocraft-cli`.
Windows uses `photocraft-0.6.0-windows-<arch>-portable.zip`
(`photocraft-cli.exe`); Linux uses `photocraft-0.6.0-linux-<arch>.tar.gz`
(`bin/photocraft-cli`). Verify downloads against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
On macOS, `codesign --verify --strict <binary>` and
`spctl --assess --type install -vv <binary>` verify its signed, notarized CLI.

Discover command IDs and parameter schemas with
`photocraft-cli commands --json --filter <word>`; they change between releases.
`photocraft-cli info <file> --compact` returns the layer tree.
`photocraft-cli run <file> --cmd <id> --params '<json>' … --out <file>`
opens, edits and saves; each `--params` belongs to the preceding `--cmd`.
`batch --actions <json> --in <dir> --out <dir>` processes folders.
`photocraft-cli mcp --automation-read-root <project> --automation-write-root <project>`
is the stdio MCP entry point; `serve` exposes JSON-lines sessions.

On macOS, 0.6.0 headlessly created and reopened a PSD, edited a type layer and
exported PNG; MCP tool discovery also worked. This does not establish Adobe
compatibility: upstream's alpha roadmap says written PSDs are not yet reliably
accepted by Photoshop. Missing fonts warn and fall back to another font.
